hasPart.name: Wild Lake is point zero for starmaking.
hasPart.text: Wild Lake is an independent studio for artists, labels, galleries and agencies. We give critical direction, fix the structure behind the work, and build the systems that carry a career. We never take ownership or a percentage.

hasPart.name: Our focus
hasPart.text: The artist: Artist Development. Support for the person behind the work and the capacity to keep making. The practice: Existential Mechanics. Aligning the life an artist leads with the work they want to build. The venture: Sovereign A&R. Sustained attention to raw material, in any form and at any stage. The structure: Creative Infrastructure. We help the world catch up to the artist, building lasting ways to encounter the work.

hasPart.name: How we work
hasPart.text: Nature is brutalist. Nothing in it is decorative, and everything carries weight. We build infrastructure for artists under that same principle. We work closely with the artist, then give them space to execute. The Method sets out our approach to critique, structural honesty, and the rhythm of an engagement.

hasPart.name: Development Protocols | Wild Lake Studio
hasPart.description: Optional artist wellbeing practices within a retained engagement, including active listening, structural honesty, automatic writing, reflection, grounding, movement, and vision quests. The artist controls participation.

hasPart.name: Reflection & Study
hasPart.text: We give the artist space to say what they have been holding, at their own pace. Our attention follows what they choose to share, allowing room for expression before interpretation or revision begins. We expose the load-bearing reality of the artist’s situation, examining what the practice can carry and where its limits are being exceeded. We call this conversational brutalism: applying the architectural principle of exposed structure to information. The conversation makes the conditions visible so the artist can decide what to change and where support is needed. Selected texts give us language for the questions emerging in the practice. Writing continuously lets associations, images, and questions emerge before editing begins. We return to the material afterward to see what it holds. Open conversation generates ideas, associations, and possible directions before we evaluate them. We return to what emerges to identify what the artist wants to explore. Articulating the future the artist wants to build, connecting intention with the choices, resources, and daily conditions that can support it. Gathering images, words, and references into a visual map of creative direction. The board becomes a shared point of reference for priorities and next steps. Images and archetypes provide prompts for interpretation, helping the artist articulate associations, tensions, and possible choices. Attentive listening becomes a study of rhythm, feeling, memory, and how a work holds attention.

hasPart.name: Attention & Grounding
hasPart.text: Steady presence, active listening, and shared attention can support nervous system settling within the working relationship. We agree together on pace, proximity, and boundaries; touch is optional and requires explicit consent. Consent remains ongoing, and the artist can pause, decline, or change direction at any time. Time to notice thoughts, sensations, and the conditions surrounding the work. Gentle attention to breathing and its relationship to movement, voice, and concentration. Self-directed contact can provide a point of physical attention. Any guided touch is discussed and agreed beforehand.

hasPart.name: Movement & Expression
hasPart.text: A change of surroundings can challenge familiar assumptions. Visits may range from a local park or the Blue Ridge Mountains to Santiago and the surrounding campo , where Argelys’s family is rooted. His experience of rural life and poverty grounds conversations about labor, access, and the conditions that sustain a creative practice. The setting and purpose are agreed with the artist. Movement offers a way to explore rhythm, impulse, pleasure, and physical expression. Voluntary movement provides another way to notice and respond to held tension. Emotion can have room without becoming an assignment. Tears, sound, or silence may emerge; none is required as evidence of progress.

hasPart.name: Operational Infrastructure
hasPart.text: We build systems that protect the artist’s attention, income, and direct audience relationships. The tools and boundaries follow the artist’s needs and agreed scope. Route professional inquiries through a structured form on the artist’s domain, using a tool such as Tally or Typeform. Require project scope, a stated budget that meets the artist’s minimum, and acknowledgment of engagement terms before an inquiry reaches the inbox. Close DMs to professional requests and direct cold contacts to the form through saved replies or email autoresponders. Build lightweight sites from portable HTML and CSS, deployed directly to an edge host such as Cloudflare Pages on the artist’s own domain. A simple static site can run without a database, framework, or build pipeline, reducing dependencies and making the work easier to maintain and move between hosts. Replace open calendar booking with an agreed request process. Require a specific agenda at least 48 hours before a proposed call, including the decision needed and relevant material. Book the meeting once its purpose is clear, protecting the artist’s time for independent work. Use payment links such as Stripe Payment Links connected to the artist’s own account, with payouts to their bank account. Send links directly to buyers or place them on the artist’s site, reducing reliance on marketplace commissions. Payment processing fees and the provider’s data handling still apply; the artist controls the offer and customer relationship. Connect a newsletter service such as Buttondown to the artist’s own domain with the required DNS records, alongside an RSS feed on their static site. Build direct subscriber relationships and retain exportable mailing lists and publishing archives, giving audiences ways to follow the work beyond platform algorithms.

hasPart.name: Within an Engagement
hasPart.text: These practices support the artist’s work within an agreed scope. Participation is voluntary, and the artist can pause, decline, or change direction. Each practice returns to a concrete question: what helps this person sustain the work they want to make? Discuss an engagement · The Method

hasPart.description: Wild-Lake’s operating manual: critique, structural honesty, artist wellbeing, sovereign ownership, and an intermittent engagement rhythm.

about.slogan: Wild-Lake is point zero for starmaking.

hasPart.name: Terms of the practice
hasPart.text: The conditions, the person, and the work. How we organize the conditions around the work—time, space, resources, habits, and boundaries—so the practice can sustain what the artist wants to make. How we develop and support the person carrying the work: their judgment, capacity, autonomy, and relationships. How we scout talent and develop creative material through critique, direction, and critical framing, while the artist retains ownership and creative control.

hasPart.name: The structural principle
hasPart.text: Nature is brutalist. Nothing in it is decorative, and everything carries weight. We build infrastructure for artists under that same principle. Clients come to Wild-Lake to build a practice or when the way they work has become unsustainable. The engagement is a controlled demolition, undertaken with the artist. We take the practice down to its studs, dismantling habits and brittle systems that can no longer carry the work. Then we rebuild around what the artist needs to operate with clarity. We dismantle the architecture of extraction. The artist survives the loop.

hasPart.name: Critique & revision
hasPart.text: At Wild-Lake, development requires close study of the material and aggressive revision with the artist. Critique is the primary mechanism of care. It demands examining the work closely enough to offer an interpretation the artist can either use as scaffolding or completely tear down. But structural stewardship requires more than artistic critique. To sustain the work, the creator must survive their own internal engine. The practice forces necessary ego deaths and dismantles narcissistic loops that drain creative stamina. We strip away the parasitic need for external supply and replace it with grounded, sovereign autonomy—killing the narcissism to protect the person, and by extension, the work. This stewardship spans across mediums, encompassing visual art, sculpture, installation, short stories, plays, scripts, essays, songs, films, and performance—as well as the macro-systems required to keep those practices standing over the long term. Audience development is part of that infrastructure. We work with artists to build publishing channels and lasting relationships with the people who encounter their work, ensuring the creator dictates the terms of engagement.

hasPart.name: Structural honesty
hasPart.text: We expose the load-bearing reality of the artist’s situation, examining what the practice can carry and where its limits are being exceeded. We call this conversational brutalism: applying the architectural principle of exposed structure to information. The conversation makes the conditions visible so the artist can decide what to change and where support is needed.

hasPart.name: Observation & absence
hasPart.text: We come close only to observe and edit, bringing absolute clarity to the raw material. Then we depart. The response, the execution, and the timeline remain entirely sovereign. We build for asynchronous stamina. Our engagement alternates between high-density structural interventions and extended periods of total absence, giving the artist the isolation required to execute without surveillance.

hasPart.name: Artist wellbeing
hasPart.text: During a retained engagement, Argelys may guide practices that bring attention to the artist’s habits, physical experience, and creative direction. We support artists healing from narcissistic abuse, examining narcissistic patterns within themselves, or navigating both. This work centers on rebuilding self-trust, recognizing harmful relational patterns, and establishing boundaries that protect creative autonomy. Building a sustainable practice can include healing from trauma and recognizing how past experiences shape the conditions of making. We make room for that history when setting the pace, boundaries, and expectations of an engagement. The artist decides what to share; our role is to support their practice, with room for care beyond the studio. Explore the practices Active listening, structural honesty, automatic writing, grounding, movement, and vision quests, alongside operational systems for inquiries, communication, payments, and direct publishing. Each practice is optional; the artist can pause, decline, or change direction.

hasPart.name: Institutional stewardship
hasPart.text: We work with curators as a defensive buffer between the artist and institutional demands. Together, we examine what an engagement asks of the artist, establish boundaries around access and output, and address pressures that could exhaust the person sustaining the work. Our role as artist developers is to make those boundaries hold.

hasPart.name: Ownership & engagement
hasPart.text: The artist retains ownership and creative control. We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative. The Stewardship Subscription reserves availability between client-triggered interventions. Response times, scope, and capacity are agreed in advance. Fixed project commissions and focused advisory engagements are also available. Engagement formats and fees · Terms of Practice

hasPart.name: Retainer terms.
hasPart.text: Focused intervention. Space to execute. The monthly Stewardship Subscription keeps studio capacity available between interventions. We come close to observe and edit, then step away while the artist executes on their own timeline. Wild-Lake takes no percentage of artist earnings or ownership of their intellectual property. The client retains ownership of their work. The Studio retains its proprietary frameworks and licenses delivered framework materials for the client’s practice. Public-facing writing transfers to the client upon final settlement. The client triggers an intervention when it is needed. We agree response times, reserved capacity, and the scope of each intervention in advance. Periods of absence are part of the engagement, giving the artist room to work independently. Their consent and creative control remain explicit throughout. The subscription is paid monthly in advance for reserved availability across the agreed cadence. Project commissions carry a fixed fee.
